examples.text: Es fisselt.

glosses: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air. (Compare fog, haze.)

examples.text: It was difficult to see through the morning mist.

glosses: A layer of fine droplets or particles.

examples.text: There was an oily mist on the lens.

glosses: Anything that dims, darkens, or hinders vision.

examples.text: His passion cast a mist before his sense.
Alas, I do not have the strength to continue writing. Already, mist veils my eyes.

glosses: To form mist.

examples.text: It's misting this morning.

glosses: To spray fine droplets on, particularly of water.

examples.text: I mist my tropical plants every morning.

glosses: To rain in very fine droplets.

examples.text: ... it's misting outside. When it mists outside it's half fog and half rain.
On this particular early morning , with a bitter cold rain misting down, Seminov was reaching the end of his endurance.
... rain misting outside from thick clouds.

glosses: To cover with a mist.

examples.text: The lens was misted.
her breath will mist or staine the stone

glosses: To be covered by tears.

examples.text: My eyes misted when I remembered what had happened.

glosses: To disperse into a mist, accompanying operation of equipment at high speeds.

examples.text: you shall be mist at Court

glosses: To rain lightly.

examples.text: We had planned a picnic for Joe's birthday, but it ended up drizzling all day.

glosses: To shed slowly in minute drops or particles.

examples.text:
And from mine eyes the drizling teares descend,
As on your boughes the ysicles depend.

glosses: To pour slowly and evenly, especially oil or honey in cooking.

examples.text: The recipe says to toss the salad and then drizzle olive oil on it.

glosses: To cover by pouring in this manner.

examples.text: The recipe says to toss the salad and then drizzle it in olive oil.

glosses: To urinate.

examples.text: She'll be right back, had to drizzle before we leave.

glosses: To carry out parfilage, the process of unravelling.

examples.text: She found that all those ladies who did not play at cards occupied their fingers with parfilage.[...] Here, the work was called drizzling. Ladies begged their friends to give them pieces of the gold lace used on uniforms and the gold tassels of sword-belts, they picked out the metal threads, and by selling these they realised considerable sums. Prince Leopold himself drizzled continually[...]

glosses: Light rain.

examples.text: Up here, it's a 'dreich' day with steady drizzle. Deep drainage channels either side of the track are already more like streams: Rannoch Moor is a wet place.

glosses: Very small, numerous, and uniformly dispersed water drops, mist, or sprinkle. Unlike fog droplets, drizzle falls to the ground.

examples.text: No longer pouring, the rain outside slowed down to a faint drizzle.

glosses: Water.

examples.text: Stop drinking all of my drizzle!

glosses: A cake onto which icing, honey or syrup has been drizzled in an artistic manner.

examples.text:
April 19, 2013,Felicity Cloake, "How to Cook the Perfect Lemon Drizzle Cake" in The Guardian
Drizzle is not normally good news. Not when it's falling from the sky, not when it's replacing a decent helping of sauce, and especially not when it's found on a menu in close proximity to the words "balsamic vinegar". Deliciously sticky, sweet and sour lemon drizzle cake is the one, and very honourable, exception.

The rest of the day is spent trying to concentrate on ingredient labels, ordering supplies, baking some fairy cakes for a hen party and two lemon drizzles, one for a new baby and one for an old dear's birthday.

glosses: A light, brief snowfall.
A sudden and brief blast or gust; a light, temporary breeze.

examples.text: a flurry of wind

When the right-away was given, Driver Gibson would give a sonorous blast on Cardean's deep-toned hooter, and amid a flurry of swirling steam the train would move majestically out, with nearly half the city of Carlisle—or so it would appear—as onlookers on the platform.

glosses: A shower of dust, leaves etc. brought on by a sudden gust of wind.
Any sudden activity; a stir.

examples.text: "I missed the beast in my flurry, but he dropped you all right and was off like a streak."

With a little manœuvring they contrived to meet on the doorstep which was […] in a boiling stream of passers-by, hurrying business people speeding past in a flurry of fumes and dust in the bright haze.

1998, Gillian Catriona Ramchand, Deconstructing the Lexicon, in Miriam Butt and Wilhelm Geuder, eds. “The Projection of Arguments”
These [argument structure] modifications are important because they have provoked a flurry of investigation into argument structure operations of merger, demotion etc.

Higglety, pigglety, pop!
The dog has eaten the mop;
The pig's in a hurry,
The cat's in a flurry,
Higglety, pigglety, pop!

The Championship highflyers almost got their reward for a resilient performance on their first visit to the Emirates, surviving a flurry of first-half Arsenal chances before hitting back with a classic sucker punch.
The day before the wedding was a flurry of preparations.

glosses: A snack consisting of soft ice cream mixed with small pieces of fruit, cookie crumbs, etc.

examples.text: Does your "Forbidden Foods" list include banana splits, ice cream sundaes, slurpies, popsicles, frozen yogurts, milk shakes, and ice cream flurries? These foods taste great but have a reputation for being bad for your health.

They will make your tongue smile with their homemade ice cream, which was voted "Best Taste in the USA Today." Enjoy exciting toppings to personalize your treat or a yummy sundae, flurry, smoothie, banana split or shake...

glosses: The violent spasms of a dying whale.

examples.text: Again and again to such gamesome talk, the dexterous dart is repeated, the spear returning to its master like a greyhound held in skilful leash. The agonized whale goes into his flurry; the tow-line is slackened, and the pitchpoler dropping astern, folds his hands, and mutely watches the monster die.

glosses: An occurrence of something (countable instances) in large numbers, happening suddenly or in a short period of time.

examples.text: The fencer landed a flurry of hits on her opponent.
The think piece provoked a flurry of media responses for the remainder of the week.

glosses: To agitate, bewilder, fluster.

examples.text: And so venturing not to say another word, poor Jemima trotted off, exceedingly flurried and nervous.
She was flurried by the term with which he had qualified her gentle friend, but she took the occasion for one to which she must in every manner lend herself.

glosses: To move or fall in a flurry.
Faire de la bruine.

examples.text: Toute la nuit encore, il avait bruiné, une poussière d’eau dont l’humidité salissait les rues.
Au dessus de ces couches de cumulo-stratus purement acqueux, il peut bruiner fortement, et même il peut pleuvoir.

Il pleuvait un peu, mais pas trop, il bruinait plutôt, de façon à donner une couleur grise aux choses et à rendre l’atmosphère mélancolique ; bref, ce temps moyen allait parfaitement avec le caractère modeste des funérailles.
Il bruinait ; le Mont-Saint-Michel abandonné des touristes se dressait solitairement entre le gris du ciel et le gris de la mer.
